examples.ko: 그 사람은 가타부타 말도 없이 나가 버렸어요.
examples.en: He walked out without saying yes or no.
Please give me a clear answer, one way or the other.
I made a proposal, but there's been no word either way yet.
He doesn't say yes or no, so it's frustrating.

examples.ko: 친구는 내 얘기를 듣고 가타부타 반응이 없었어요.
examples.en: My friend heard my story and showed no reaction either way.

examples.ko: 싫으면 싫다고, 가타부타 확실히 말해 줘요.
examples.en: If you don't like it, say so; tell me clearly either way.

explain: '가타부타 말이 없다', '가타부타 대답이 없다'처럼 주로 부정하는 말과 함께 써서 답답하거나 서운한 마음을 나타내요. 좋다 나쁘다 의견을 분명히 말하지 않는 상대에게 쓰는 말투예요. 조사 없이 그대로 부사처럼 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 부장님은 제 제안에 가타부타 말이 없으세요.
phrases.en: My manager says neither yes nor no to my proposal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 의견을 분명히 말하지 않는 사람이 답답할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone doesn't state an opinion clearly and it's frustrating.

phrases.en: I've had no answer either way for days, and it's frustrating.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연락이나 질문에 답이 오지 않을 때 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can be used when a message or question goes unanswered.
phrases.en_equiv: to give no answer either way

phrases.en: I wish you'd tell me yes or no first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 분명한 대답을 요구할 때 쓰는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A way of asking for a clear answer.

explain_en: It is usually used with negative phrases, as in '가타부타 말이 없다' or '가타부타 대답이 없다', to show frustration or disappointment. It is aimed at someone who won't say clearly whether they agree or not. It is often used without a particle, almost like an adverb.

en: official post; title (originally a traditional hat)

examples.en: My father took the position of president at the alumni association.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 감투가 탐나서 선거에 나왔대요.
examples.en: I heard he ran in the election because he wanted the title.
Even though it's a small group, the fight over positions is fierce.

examples.ko: 감투에 욕심내지 말고 맡은 일부터 잘하세요.
examples.en: Don't be greedy for titles; do the work you've been given well first.
What's the point of wearing a title that's in name only?
I'm just an ordinary employee at my company without any title.

explain: 원래는 예전에 머리에 쓰던 모자 이름인데, 지금은 대부분 '높은 자리, 직책'을 가리키는 말로 써요. 대개 자리에 대한 욕심을 조금 비꼬는 느낌이 있어서 '감투 싸움', '감투 욕심'처럼 말해요. 좋은 뜻으로 점잖게 말할 때는 '직책'이나 '자리'를 써요.

phrases.example: 친구가 동호회 회장 감투를 쓰더니 바빠졌어요.
phrases.en: My friend became the club president and got busy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모자를 쓴다는 뜻이 아니라 회장 같은 직책을 맡게 된다는 뜻이에요. 조금 놀리듯 말할 때가 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: It doesn't mean putting on a hat; it means taking on a post like president. It is often said in a slightly teasing way.
phrases.en_equiv: take on a title; land a position

explain_en: It was originally the name of a hat worn on the head long ago, but now it mostly means a high post or title. It often has a slightly sarcastic tone about craving status, as in '감투 싸움' and '감투 욕심'. For a neutral or polite tone, use '직책' or '자리'.

examples.ko: 어린 시절 우리 집은 늘 궁핍했어요.
examples.en: My family was always poor when I was a child.

examples.ko: 궁핍한 살림에도 부모님은 저를 학교에 보냈어요.
examples.en: Even in hard times, my parents sent me to school.
After I lost my job, life gradually became harder and poorer.
I helped a neighbor who was so poor that they skipped meals.

examples.ko: 마음이 궁핍하지 않은 사람이 진짜 부자예요.
examples.en: A person whose heart is not poor is the truly rich one.

examples.ko: 그는 궁핍하게 살면서도 늘 웃음을 잃지 않았어요.
examples.en: Even while living in poverty, he never lost his smile.

explain: '가난하다'보다 딱딱한 글말에 가깝고, 돈이나 물건이 모자라 살림이 어려운 형편을 말할 때 써요. '궁핍한 생활', '살림이 궁핍하다'처럼 자주 짝을 이루고, '마음이 궁핍하다'처럼 비유로도 써요. 반대말은 '풍족하다', '넉넉하다'예요.

phrases.example: 전쟁 뒤에 사람들은 궁핍한 생활을 했어요.
phrases.en: After the war, people lived in poverty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 형용사 활용형 '궁핍한'으로 생활을 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form 궁핍한 describes a way of life.

phrases.en: Our household is hard up these days, so I'm worried.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈이 모자라 집안 형편이 어려울 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for a household short on money.

phrases.en: In those days everyone lived in poverty.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게'로 활용하면 어떻게 사는지 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The -게 form tells how one lives.

explain_en: It is closer to a stiff, written word than '가난하다', and it describes a hard situation where money or goods fall short. It pairs naturally with '궁핍한 생활' and '살림이 궁핍하다', and can also be used figuratively, as in '마음이 궁핍하다'. Its opposites are '풍족하다' and '넉넉하다'.

examples.en: I was so nervous that I swallowed hard.
I stayed up all night playing games.

examples.ko: 해가 꼴딱 넘어가기 전에 집에 가요.
examples.en: Let's go home before the sun sets.
I gulped down the medicine, but the bitter taste lingers.

examples.ko: 친구와 수다를 떠느라 날을 꼴딱 샜어요.
examples.en: I stayed up all night chatting with my friend.

examples.ko: 아이가 마지막 한 모금을 꼴딱 마셨어요.
examples.en: The child gulped down the last sip.

explain: '꼴깍'처럼 침이나 음식을 삼키는 소리로 쓰지만, '밤을 꼴딱 새우다'에서는 잠을 한숨도 못 자고 밤을 보낸다는 뜻이 돼요. 이 표현은 통째로 외워 두세요.

phrases.en: I stayed up all night studying for the exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잠을 한숨도 못 자고 밤을 보냈다는 뜻이에요. '밤을 새우다'를 더 생생하게 말하는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means you spent the night without sleeping at all. It sounds more vivid than plain '밤을 새우다'.

explain_en: Like '꼴깍', it is the sound of swallowing saliva or food, but in '밤을 꼴딱 새우다' it means spending the night without sleeping at all. Learn that expression as a whole.

examples.en: They say heroes appear in troubled times.

examples.ko: 영화 속 주인공은 난세를 살아가는 평범한 사람이에요.
examples.en: The main character in the movie is an ordinary person living through turbulent times.
The more troubled the times, the more you feel how precious family is.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 난세의 백성들 이야기를 다뤄요.
examples.en: This novel deals with the stories of common people in turbulent times.

examples.ko: 난세에 태어난 사람들은 힘든 삶을 살았어요.
examples.en: People born in troubled times lived hard lives.

examples.ko: 사람들은 요즘 같은 때를 난세라고 말하기도 해요.
examples.en: Some people call times like these turbulent times.

explain: 전쟁이나 혼란으로 어지러운 시대를 말하고, 반대로 평화로운 때는 '태평성대'라고 해요. 역사, 사극, 소설에 많이 나오고 '난세에 영웅 난다'라는 말로도 자주 들어요.

phrases.en: He was called a hero of troubled times.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어지러운 시대에 나타나 큰일을 한 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to someone who rose to greatness in chaotic times.

phrases.en: My grandmother lived through the turbulent time of war.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘든 시대를 지나며 살았다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to have lived through a hard era.

phrases.en: In troubled times, people feel anxious.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '에는'을 붙여 그런 시대의 일반적인 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With the particle 에는, used to describe what is typical of such times.

explain_en: It refers to an era disordered by war or chaos; a peaceful era is '태평성대'. It appears often in history, historical dramas and novels, and in the saying '난세에 영웅 난다' (heroes arise in troubled times).

examples.en: My legs shake when I stand at the edge of the cliff.
While walking on the mountain path, I looked down below the cliff.
Be careful, there is a cliff right ahead.
A big rock rolled down from the cliff.

examples.ko: 벼랑 위에 작은 집 한 채가 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small house on top of the cliff.

examples.ko: 그 팀은 마지막 경기에서 벼랑 끝으로 몰렸어요.
examples.en: That team was pushed to the brink in the last game.

explain: '절벽'과 비슷하지만 '벼랑'은 우리말다운 느낌이 강하고, 위험한 상황을 비유할 때 특히 잘 써요. 보통 '벼랑 끝'이라는 형태로 많이 나와요.

phrases.example: 갑자기 매출이 줄어서 회사가 벼랑 끝에 몰렸어요.
phrases.en: Sales suddenly dropped, and the company was pushed to the brink.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 물러설 곳 없는 아주 위험한 상황에 놓였다는 뜻의 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figure of speech for being in a very dangerous situation with nowhere left to retreat.

explain_en: It is close to '절벽' (cliff), but '벼랑' feels more native Korean and is especially common in figurative talk about danger. It often appears in the form '벼랑 끝'.

examples.ko: 오늘 경기는 지난 패배를 갚는 설욕전이에요.
examples.en: Today's match is a rematch to make up for the last defeat.

examples.ko: 두 팀의 설욕전에 관중이 가득 찼어요.
examples.en: The crowd filled the stadium for the two teams' revenge match.
That player was nervous ahead of the revenge match.
It's a rematch for last year's final, so I'm even more excited.
After winning the revenge match, the whole team cheered.

examples.ko: 이번 설욕전은 꼭 이겨야 한다고 감독이 말했어요.
examples.en: The coach said we must win this revenge match.

explain: 전에 졌던 상대와 다시 만나 겨루는 경기를 말해요. 스포츠 뉴스 제목에 자주 나오고, 외래어로는 '리턴 매치'라고도 해요.

phrases.example: 두 팀은 다음 주에 설욕전을 치러요.
phrases.en: The two teams will play a revenge match next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: '치르다'는 경기를 한다는 뜻이라서 '설욕전'과 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: 치르다 means holding a match, so it pairs well with 설욕전.

phrases.example: 그 선수는 작년 우승자와 설욕전에 나섰어요.
phrases.en: That player stepped up for a rematch against last year's winner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직접 다시 겨루러 나서는 선수나 팀을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for a player or team stepping up to compete again.
phrases.en_equiv: to take part in a revenge match

phrases.en: A rematch will be held in the final.
phrases.nuance_ko: 외래어로 같은 뜻이고, 일상 대화에서도 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is a loanword with the same meaning, common in everyday talk too.

explain_en: It is a match against an opponent who beat you before. It often appears in sports headlines, and the loanword '리턴 매치' (return match) is also used.

examples.ko: 설혹 비가 와도 우리는 출발할 거예요.
examples.en: Even if it rains, we will set off.
Even if you're wrong, try saying it.

examples.ko: 설혹 늦게 도착한다 해도 걱정하지 마세요.
examples.en: Even if I arrive late, please don't worry.

examples.ko: 설혹 그 말이 사실이라 해도 저는 믿기 어려워요.
examples.en: Even if that is true, it's hard for me to believe.
Even if I fail, I won't give up.

examples.ko: 설혹 가격이 좀 비싸다 해도 이 가방을 사고 싶어요.
examples.en: Even if the price is a bit high, I want to buy this bag.

explain: 뒤에 '-더라도', '-ㄴ다 해도', '-ㄹ지라도'처럼 '그렇다 해도'라는 뜻의 표현이 같이 와요. '설령'과 거의 같은 뜻이고, 조금 더 글에 어울려요. 말할 때는 '아무리 ~어도'로 바꿔 말하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: Even if you are late, please come.
phrases.nuance_ko: '설혹'과 거의 같은 뜻이고, '설령'이 말과 글에서 더 두루 쓰여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly identical to 설혹, but 설령 is used more broadly in both speech and writing.

phrases.en: Even if it is hard, don't give up.
phrases.nuance_ko: '설혹'은 뒤에 '-더라도'를 붙여 '그렇다 해도'라는 뜻을 만들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: 설혹 pairs with '-더라도' to mean 'even if that is the case'.

phrases.en: No matter how busy I am, I eat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때는 '설혹' 대신 이 표현을 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In speech, people use this pattern more often than 설혹.

explain_en: It is followed by concessive endings such as '-더라도', '-ㄴ다 해도' and '-ㄹ지라도'. It means almost the same as '설령' and suits writing a bit more. In speech people often switch to '아무리 ~어도'.

examples.en: Our team won three games in a row.
If we keep winning, we can take the title.
That player is on a winning run this year.
We won consecutively, so our ranking went up a lot.
Can we keep winning this weekend too?

examples.ko: 연승하고 싶어서 선수들이 더 열심히 뛰어요.
examples.en: The players run harder because they want to keep winning.

explain: 스포츠 경기에서 이기는 일이 계속 이어질 때 써요. 한 번만 이겼다면 '이기다'를 써요. 반대말은 '연패하다'예요. 보통 '세 경기를 연승하다'처럼 횟수와 같이 말해요.

phrases.en: Our team is winning consecutively right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이기는 일이 지금도 이어지는 중일 때 쓰는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A conjugated form used when the winning is still going on.
phrases.en_equiv: to be on a winning streak

phrases.en: This time we couldn't win in a row.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 번 이긴 뒤 다음 경기에서 이기지 못했을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a team won once but couldn't win the next game.

phrases.example: 우리 팀이 두 경기를 연이어 이겼어요.
phrases.en: Our team won two games in a row.
phrases.nuance_ko: '연승하다'와 뜻이 같은 쉬운 말이에요. 일상 대화에서 쓰기 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier phrase with the same meaning as '연승하다', good for everyday conversation.

explain_en: Use it when wins keep coming one after another in sports. For a single win, just say '이기다'. The opposite is '연패하다'. People usually give a count, as in '세 경기를 연승하다'.

examples.en: The match was tied, so it went into extra time.
Our team won after extra time.
If it goes to extra time, your stamina drops a lot.
The winning goal came in extra time.
If the score is still tied in extra time, there is a penalty shootout.

examples.ko: 지난 시즌에는 연장전이 많아서 선수들이 힘들어했어요.
examples.en: Last season had many extra-time games, so the players had a hard time.

explain: 정해진 시간 안에 승부가 나지 않을 때 더 하는 경기가 '연장전'이에요. 야구에서는 '연장 10회'처럼 회로 말하고, 축구에서는 연장전에서도 비기면 '승부차기'로 넘어가요.

phrases.en: Yesterday's game went to overtime.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정해진 시간에 끝나지 않았다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it did not finish in regular time.

phrases.en: The two teams played ten minutes of extra time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 하는 경기를 실제로 한다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the extra match is actually played.

phrases.en: Our team lost in overtime.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이기다'와 바꿔서 결과를 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can swap with 이기다 to say the result.

explain_en: A '연장전' is the extra play when no winner is decided in the set time. In baseball people say '연장 10회' (the 10th inning of extras), and in soccer a tie after extra time goes to '승부차기' (penalties).

examples.en: I got through the audition's preliminary screening safely.
Last year I failed the preliminary round, which was a real shame.

examples.ko: 내일 아침 아홉 시에 예심이 열려요.
examples.en: The preliminary screening takes place tomorrow at nine in the morning.
The participants in the preliminary round get number tags and wait.

examples.ko: 이번 예심에는 천 명이 넘게 지원했어요.
examples.en: Over a thousand people applied for this preliminary screening.
The preliminary screening of this contest is held privately.

explain: 본선에 올라갈 사람을 먼저 가려내는 심사예요. '예선'은 경기에서 많이 쓰고, '예심'은 오디션이나 공모전처럼 심사로 가리는 곳에서 자주 써요. 짝이 되는 말은 '본선'이에요.

phrases.en: My friend passed the preliminary round of the singing contest.
phrases.nuance_ko: '예심'과 함께 결과를 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used to talk about the result of a preliminary screening.

phrases.example: 많은 참가자가 예심을 거쳐 본선에 올라가요.
phrases.en: Many contestants go through the preliminary round and advance to the finals.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예심을 지나 다음 단계로 간다는 흐름을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows moving on to the next stage after the preliminary round.

phrases.en: Our team won in the qualifying round.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경기에서 본선에 갈 팀을 가리는 단계를 말하고, 심사로 가리는 '예심'과 구별해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The qualifying stage in games; unlike '예심', which is judged by screening.

explain_en: It is the first screening that picks who goes on to the main round. '예선' is common for sports matches, while '예심' is often used for judged events such as auditions and contests. Its counterpart is '본선' (the main round).

examples.ko: 번역가가 이 문장의 뜻을 오역해서 독자들이 오해했어요.
examples.en: The translator mistranslated the meaning of this sentence, so readers misunderstood.
If you translate in a hurry, it's easy to mistranslate words.
There's a part in the subtitles where a joke was mistranslated.

examples.ko: 제가 이 부분을 오역했는지 확인해 주세요.
examples.en: Please check whether I mistranslated this part.
Machine translation sometimes mistranslates proverbs.

examples.ko: 오역하지 않으려면 앞뒤 문맥을 잘 봐야 해요.
examples.en: To avoid mistranslating, you have to look closely at the context.

explain: '잘못 번역하다'와 같은 뜻이고, 책이나 영화 자막, 기사 번역 이야기를 할 때 많이 나와요. 명사 '오역'은 '오역이 많다'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 문장을 잘못 번역해서 뜻이 완전히 달라졌어요.
phrases.en: I translated the sentence wrongly, so the meaning changed completely.
phrases.nuance_ko: '오역하다'와 같은 뜻이고, 일상 대화에서 더 쉽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This means the same as 오역하다 and is easier to use in everyday talk.

phrases.example: 한 단어를 오역하는 바람에 이야기가 이상해졌어요.
phrases.en: Because I mistranslated one word, the story became strange.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는 바람에'를 붙여 오역이 나쁜 결과의 이유가 되었다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -는 바람에, it says the mistranslation was the reason for a bad result.

phrases.en: This movie's subtitles have a lot of mistranslations.
phrases.nuance_ko: '오역하다'의 명사 형태로, 잘못된 번역 그 자체를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the noun form of 오역하다 and refers to the wrong translation itself.

explain_en: It means the same as '잘못 번역하다' (to translate wrongly) and often comes up when talking about books, movie subtitles or translated articles. The noun '오역' is used like '오역이 많다' (there are many mistranslations).

examples.ko: 황무지를 몇 년 가꿔서 옥토로 바꿨어요.
examples.en: They worked the wasteland for a few years and turned it into fertile land.

examples.ko: 이 마을은 강 옆이라 땅이 옥토예요.
examples.en: This village is next to a river, so the land is fertile.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 거친 땅을 옥토로 만들려고 평생 일하셨어요.
examples.en: My grandfather worked his whole life to turn rough land into rich farmland.

examples.ko: 옥토에서 자란 쌀이라 맛이 정말 좋아요.
examples.en: This rice was grown in fertile soil, so it tastes really good.

examples.ko: 농부들은 모두 옥토를 차지하고 싶어 했어요.
examples.en: All the farmers wanted to get hold of the fertile land.

examples.ko: 돌밭이 옥토가 되기까지 시간이 오래 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a long time for the stony field to become fertile land.

explain: '비옥한 땅'과 같은 뜻이지만 '옥토'가 더 짧고 글에서 많이 보여요. '황무지'와 짝으로 '황무지를 옥토로 만들다'처럼 힘들게 일군 땅을 말할 때 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: There is a lot of fertile land near the river.
phrases.nuance_ko: '옥토'와 같은 뜻이고, 말할 때 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 옥토, and sounds more natural in speech.

phrases.en: The farmers turned the dry land into rich soil.
phrases.nuance_ko: 애써서 땅을 좋게 바꾼다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the feeling of working hard to make land good.

phrases.example: 몇 년 뒤에 그곳은 옥토가 되었어요.
phrases.en: A few years later, that place became fertile soil.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땅이 좋게 바뀐 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say the result of land becoming good.

explain_en: It means the same as '비옥한 땅' (rich land), but '옥토' is shorter and often seen in writing. It pairs with '황무지' (wasteland), as in '황무지를 옥토로 만들다', when talking about land made good through hard work.

examples.en: Our team was completely beaten in the final.

examples.ko: 아무리 준비해도 상대가 강하면 완패할 수 있어요.
examples.en: No matter how much you prepare, you can be totally beaten if the opponent is strong.
We lost badly in the first game, so the mood dropped.
Even after a crushing loss, the players smiled and shook hands.
I ended up getting totally beaten by my younger sibling in the game.
On the day of the crushing loss, I didn't even want to eat.

explain: 점수나 실력 차이가 커서 크게 졌다는 뜻이에요. 반대는 '완승하다'이고, 같은 방향으로 '완파하다'는 이긴 쪽 입장에서 써요. 지는 쪽 입장에서는 '완패하다', 이기는 쪽 입장에서는 '완파하다'가 돼요.

phrases.en: Our team lost badly in yesterday's game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 끝난 경기의 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to report the result of a game that is already over.

phrases.en: We were not prepared enough, so we ended up losing badly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 말았어요'를 붙이면 안타깝다는 느낌이 더해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-go marasseoyo' gives a sense of regret.

phrases.example: 우리 팀이 큰 점수 차로 대패했어요.
phrases.en: Our team lost by a big margin.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하고, 점수 차가 크게 난 패배에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning, for a loss by a big score gap.
phrases.en_equiv: to lose by a big margin

explain_en: It means losing badly because the gap in score or skill is big. The opposite is '완승하다', and '완파하다' describes the same game from the winner's side: the loser '완패하다', the winner '완파하다'.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 지구의 종말을 다루고 있어요.
examples.en: That movie deals with the end of the Earth.
The end of the dictatorship is near.
I read the story of an empire that met its end.

examples.ko: 그는 인류의 종말을 걱정하는 책을 썼어요.
examples.en: He wrote a book worrying about the end of humanity.
The end of that city began with a war.
A rumor spread that the end of the world was coming.

explain: '끝'은 가장 평범한 말이고, '종말'은 큰 것이 완전히 끝나고 사라지는 무거운 느낌이에요. 그래서 '세상의 종말', '제국의 종말'처럼 큰 대상에 어울려요. 하루나 수업이 끝나는 일에는 쓰지 않아요. 비슷한 말 '최후'는 죽음이나 마지막 순간에 더 쓰여요.

phrases.en: That kingdom finally met its end.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 것이 완전히 끝난다는 뜻으로 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing meaning something big comes to a complete end.

phrases.en: I read a novel about the end of the world.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영화나 소설에서 자주 나오는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An expression that often appears in movies and novels.

phrases.en: Will the Earth also come to an end someday?
phrases.nuance_ko: 끝나는 때가 다가온다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means that the time of the end is coming.

explain_en: 끝 is the plain word for end; 종말 carries a heavy sense of something large ending and disappearing, as in 세상의 종말 (end of the world) or 제국의 종말. It would be odd for the end of a day or class. A similar word, 최후, leans toward death or the last moment.

dis.h: Final destruction or end, like the world's

p.n: 말기 is a last period or stage, not the destruction of the world.

en: to be turbid; to be muddy

examples.en: It rained, so the river water is muddy.
The air was so stuffy that I opened the window.
It is hard for fish to live in murky water.
The mood of the election must not become corrupted.
When my mind feels clouded, I take a walk.
Many people feel that politics is murky and unclean.

explain: 물이나 공기가 흐릴 때뿐 아니라 정치, 사회, 분위기가 어지럽고 깨끗하지 않을 때도 써요. 반대말은 '맑다'나 '깨끗하다'예요. 일상에서 물이나 공기를 말할 때는 '탁하다'가 더 쉬워요.

phrases.en: It's hard for fish to live in murky water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 흐리고 깨끗하지 않은 물을 글에서 점잖게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal, written way to describe cloudy, unclean water.

phrases.en: The mood around the election grew murkier.
phrases.nuance_ko: 분위기나 사회가 어지럽고 나쁘게 변할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used when an atmosphere or society grows chaotic and corrupt.

phrases.en: The air was stuffy, so I opened the window.
phrases.nuance_ko: 혼탁하다보다 쉬워서 일상에서 물이나 공기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than 혼탁하다, used in daily life for water or air.

explain_en: It describes not only cloudy water or air but also politics, society or atmosphere that is messy and not clean. Its opposites are '맑다' and '깨끗하다'. For water or air in daily talk, '탁하다' is easier.

examples.ko: 이 땅은 오랫동안 황무지로 남아 있었어요.
examples.en: This land remained a wasteland for a long time.
They began planting trees on the barren land.
He turned the wasteland into a field.
There was only wind on the wasteland, and nothing else.
The village everyone left became a wasteland.
We started over in a place like a wasteland.

explain: 농사를 짓지 않고 버려 둔 거친 땅에 써요. '황무지에서 꽃을 피우다'처럼 아무것도 없는 곳에서 성과를 낸다는 비유로도 자주 써요. '사막'은 모래와 건조한 기후 때문에 생긴 땅이라 다른 말이에요.

phrases.example: 불이 난 뒤에 숲이 황무지가 됐어요.
phrases.en: After the fire, the forest became a wasteland.
phrases.nuance_ko: 좋았던 땅이 거칠게 변했다고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when good land has turned rough and barren.

phrases.en: He made something bloom in a wasteland.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아무것도 없는 곳에서 성과를 냈다는 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figure of speech for succeeding where there was nothing.

phrases.en: Grass grew on the abandoned land.
phrases.nuance_ko: '황무지'를 쉽게 풀어서 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy way to say 황무지 in plain words.

explain_en: It is used for rough land left unfarmed. It is also often used figuratively, as in '황무지에서 꽃을 피우다', for achieving something where there was nothing. '사막' is land formed by sand and a dry climate, so it is a different word.
